title: Name the review carve-out where the rule itself lives
action:
A rule with an unnamed exception misleads everyone who reads it. Two files carry that rule and must now carry its one exception.

**1. `AGENTS.md`.** Find the line that states independent review is user-invoked (it reads roughly 'Independent review is a separate, user-invoked pass, never an automatic stage of that chain'). Leave the rule standing and add ONE sentence naming its single exception: inside the bee-herding cockpit, and only while the owner's enable marker exists AND `gate_bypass` is `full` or `total`, the `route` role may start a reviewer on a different agent without being asked (decision 8388df3e). Everywhere else the rule is unchanged. Keep it to one sentence — AGENTS.md is always-loaded context and every word costs every session.

**2. `skills/bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md`.** This file is where each cockpit safety boundary has its full record. Add route's boundary beside the existing ones, in their shape and at their length: the carve-out and its two owner-held arming conditions; that route can never arm itself because both conditions are the owner's; that the reviewer must run on a different `herding.agents` entry and refuses rather than guessing; that route never merges, never approves a gate, never starts a coder and never creates a pane; and that the in-review marker is the mechanism keeping merge off a worktree mid-review.

Both edits describe behavior slice 2 actually ships. Do not describe anything else.
verify: rg -q 'route' AGENTS.md && rg -q 'gate_bypass' AGENTS.md && rg -q 'route' skills/bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md && rg -q 'bee-herding.review' skills/bee-herding/references/operational-invariants.md

truths: the AGENTS.md rule still stands and gains exactly one sentence naming the exception and its two arming conditions
operational-invariants.md carries route's boundary at the length and shape its siblings use
both name the different-agent requirement and the refusal direction
neither describes behavior slice 2 does not ship
